documents.population: First-year international students (secondary education outside the U.S.) applying to UC San Diego, including Computer Science
documents.notes: UC San Diego Undergraduate Admissions 'International Students' page. A standing page; no year is printed on the list. The required records are country-specific ('Required Documents' per country in the page's U.S. High School Diploma Equivalents selector, e.g. China: grade 9-12 records and the graduation certificate (Red Book); India: attested Statement of Marks for STD X and XII) and are sent after admission, directly from the school or an approved e-transcript vendor (Digitary, Parchment, CHESICC), by July 1 (IB scores by July 15). Applicants self-report all completed coursework in the application. 'UC San Diego will not consider SAT or ACT test scores as a factor in admissions decisions.' The UC application and Personal Insight Questions are not named on this page and are not drafted.

items.quote: To be considered for admission to UC San Diego, international students must meet specific English proficiency requirements. Applying as a First-Year International Student The tests listed below are all accepted to showcase English proficiency.
items.notes: Accepted: TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic (7), AP English Language/Literature (3-5), IB English A, Duolingo (115).

items.quote: Your admission to UC San Diego is provisional pending the receipt and review of your official transcripts, records and exam results.
items.condition: newly admitted first-year students who attended a school outside the United States: official records from grade 9 onward, sent directly by the school or an approved e-transcript vendor by July 1, as listed for the applicant's country

items.quote: To be granted a visa, international students must prove sufficient funds to meet all expenses for studying in the U.S.
items.condition: international students who need a student visa
